 Denmark vs Norway (Tuesday, 19:45) 
 An entertaining contest looks likely when Denmark go up against Norway in the Nations League on Tuesday night.
 The Danes will come into this clash brimming with confidence after claiming a stunning 4-1 win away to Portugal on Saturday, a result that means Brian Riemer’s side only need to avoid defeat to secure a place in the quarter-finals.
 Norway can still overtake them, but must win by three goals, which should make for an open game.
 With both teams finding the net in all five of Norway’s Nations League matches so far, including their thrilling 3-2 win over Denmark, BTTS looks worthy of support once again.
 The same selection has also proven profitable in three of the hosts’ five games, adding weight to the case for another high-scoring shootout in this Scandinavian showdown.
 Wales vs Portugal (Tuesday, 19:45) 
 Portugal will be looking to return to winning ways in the Nations League when they conclude their group campaign against Wales on Tuesday night. 
 Jorge Jesus’ side had won four games in succession before that run came to an abrupt end with a shock 4-1 defeat at home to Denmark on Saturday.
 Despite that setback, the Selecao remain top of the group and will secure first place by taking a point or better in Cardiff.
 Wales, meanwhile, will finish bottom after Saturday’s 3-1 defeat away to Norway, but Craig Bellamy’s side are unlikely to roll over and could make their mark against a Portugal team that has looked far from watertight.
 The visitors have failed to keep a clean sheet in each of their last four matches, with both teams scoring in every one of those games.
 BTTS has also landed in two of Wales’ last three matches, so a repeat looks worth siding with in the Welsh capital.
 Poland vs Sweden (Tuesday, 19:45) 
 Two teams with different priorities meet at the Tarczynski Arena on Tuesday night as Poland host Sweden.
 Jan Urban’s hosts remain at risk of relegation after a 2-1 defeat away to Romania last time out.
 Sweden, meanwhile, have already secured top spot after winning four of their five group games, so Graham Potter’s men can afford to take their foot off the gas.
 That could lead to an open encounter, with BTTS landing in all five of Sweden’s matches so far, including their 3-1 win over Poland in the reverse fixture.
 The same selection also landed in Poland’s last outing, so a repeat looks worth siding with on matchday six.
